steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Rinse salmon, and arrange in a 9x13 inch baking dish. Sprinkle salt, pepper, onion powder, and dill over the fish. Place pieces of butter evenly over the fish.
Bake in preheated oven for 20 to 25 minutes. Salmon is done when it flakes easily with a fork.

raw_recipe.headline: Salmon with Dill
raw_recipe.description: Baked salmon with onion powder and dried dill weed. With just a hint of seasoning, you can make salmon taste delicious.
raw_recipe.name: Salmon with Dill

review.reviewBody:
salmon and dill...outstanding...I like garlic, but onion is good too. ONLY cook til opaque...400 for 25 minutes is way long oftimes....use two forks to pull apart at 10 minutes, and likely it is opaque already...if not add 1-2 minutes as needed. overcooked fish are dry and tasteless. needs to be cooked very carefully. The thicker, the longer...tail pieces of salmon are best tasting and cook quicker. Try sour cream/mayo half and half plus fresh dill as a sauce, yummm...

John

I eat Salmon not because I want to, but because I have to. This recipe, however, makes me want to! Made a few changes, all based on tips I read in several reviews on Allrecipes. First, soaking the Salmon in lemon juice for 20 minutes took away the ‘fishy’ taste. When seasoning, I added garlic powder to the ingredients already suggested here. Next, I cooked the Salmon on the BBQ grill over medium-high heat, starting with the skin side down on aluminum foil. After 7 minutes, flipped the Salmon by just flipping the foil over by grasping the long edge of the foil, turning the Salmon to grill directly over the heat, and then removing the foil, which also easily pulled the skin away from the fish, with the foil sticking to the skin. After removing the skin, I hit it with some more butter and dill and let it grill for another 7 minutes. Topped the Salmon with a dill sauce, made from equal parts sour cream and mayonnaise with fresh dill mixed in. My wife, who is also not a huge fan of Salmon, said this was the best she’s ever had and would welcome it any night of the week.

Seared for two minutes on each side in my cast iron pan, & then pressed fresh garlic (made red onions & mushrooms on the side), sprinkled dill, pats of butter, and red cooking wine before placing in the oven for 15 minutes. I prefer the doneness more or less towards medium.

I would never bake salmon for 25 minutes, that's way too long. It would be like cardboard. 
I've been making salmon like this for quite awhile, however, I don't add garlic or onion powder to it. 
 I always use salmon filet. On both sides, sprinkle a little Kosher salt, lemon pepper, dill and a sliver of butter and bake at 400 degrees for 10 minutes. Perfect every time. My husband likes it a little crispy, so using the same recipe, I saute the salmon in a pan with just a small amount of butter atop the gas range. Very good either way.

I made this pretty much exactly as directed, except that I melted the butter & blended the herbs/spices into it. In the future there's two things I'd do differently: 1. I'd definitely cut down on the pepper and maybe the dill as well. 2. I'd follow the '10 min per inch of fish' rule--I checked on this at 15 minutes and it was really rather overdone.

One of the BEST salmon recipes I've ever had & a high class restaurant quality. After reading the reviews these are the changes I made; drizzled the salmon filets with lemon juice, sprinkled with garlic powder, dried dill, salt & pepper. Smothered the filets with light mayo. & sprinkled with more dill & 1 cup of chopped green onions. Pressed the mayo, dill & green onions on to the fillets with a back of a spoon to make sure it adhered. Baked at 400 for 25 min. Served it with baked potatoes, saluted zucchini & green salad.

Made it on Cedar plank on the BBQ, and was great! The only thing I changed where the times, I followed the planks instructions: After the BBQ was pre-heated on high, place the planks on medium for 5 minutes closing the BBQ lid until the planks begin smoking, leave them smoke for a few minutes (have a water spray bottle handy to douse flames in planks), then lower the flames to lowest and leave another 15-18 minutes until salmon flaky with a fork.

Turned out great! I went with one of the reviewers who sautéed the onions, butter, dill, and I used fresh 3 cloves of fresh garlic minced and poured it over the fish like she had done. It took about 20mins at 400F in a non convection oven. Enjoy!!

I use half the butter and squeeze lemon juice over the salmon. I also find I only need 12-15 minutes for a 3 pound (pretty thick) salmon. I have made this recipe at least a dozen times and it never disappoints!

I love this recipe and make it whenever I want fish. I have made slight changes on the recipe tho. I add chopped garlic on the salmon instead of onion powder and use always fresh dill. I don’t add pepper. I find the foil cleaner way to use so I always cook in foil and every time it turns out well cooked delicious dish. I serve with extra lemon juice, chopped onion and cappers to garnish. ??
I cooked it on the grill in foil. 5 min. each side. I used fresh dill and onion and used olive oil instead of butter.

I made this for tonight's dinner. It was quick and easy. I made John's dill sauce to go with it, and, it added just the right flavor to the salmon. See John's suggestion in the reviews. The sauce is simple to make as well.
I squeezed half a lemon over salmon and put thinly sliced onions on top. Came out great.
Easy and tasty recipe.

Fresh dill would have been better, but I wanted to follow the recipe. I would definitely cut back on the dried dill next time, as it was overpowering and gave the fish an almost grassy flavor. I would also reverse the salt and pepper amounts (too much pepper, not enough salt), but otherwise this smelled great while cooking. The milk solids in the butter do tend to burn at such a high temp, so keep an eye on it. 16 minutes was plenty long for my liking. It was cook thoroughly, and still moist.

Wow, this was amazing! I only had a small piece so I just sprinkled the ingredients on both sides and put it in a glass pan into my air fryer. I did use the bake button and actually I checked on it at 16 minutes and took it out. Might even could have taken it out at 12-14 mins. So easy. Beautiful and tasty.
Maybe I went too light on the seasonings because this was pretty bland. I marinated for 45 minutes, also.

This is an excellent preparation for my farm-raised Norwegian salmon. I mostly followed the instructions but, as others have noted, baked at 450 degrees for 12 minutes (my salmon was an inch thick). I served this with some lemon juice and homemade tartar sauce from this site (Tartar Sauce I), which really added to the dish but isn't totally necessary as it's good enough on its own. I did find the fish quite buttery and would maybe cut down on it a bit or try mayo next time.

I followed other recommendations and: marinated it in lemon juice (I squeezed one whole lemon), used fresh dill, substituted mayo for the butter, and monitored the done-ness after 10 minutes. It was quite delish, tasted sorta like it already had tartar sauce on it.
I added more butter but I only did because I had more salmon. This is a delicious recipe.
